To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the high rotation speeds can effectively weaken the tool/work-piece interaction during friction stir welding of dissimilar Al Cu plates, and the joints produced at 2500 3000 rpm exhibit higher fracture loads than the ones fabricated at 3500 4000 rpm.

the Al Cu joints fabricated by high rotation speed FSW without tool penetration into Cu sheets exhibit large Al Cu coexistence zone, where the interfacial microstructures and the mechanical performance can be tailored by varying rotation speeds.
high rotation speed FSW can produce large size Al Cu coexisting zones at the Al Cu joint interface, which is beneficial to improve the joint strength.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the formation of Al Cu coexistence zone and the effect of rotation speeds on the structure property characteristics of Al and Cu lap joints produced by high rotation speed FSW, and the obtained results are expected to provide a new approach for FSW of dissimilar materials.
a new approach to friction stir lap welding dissimilar metals without tool penetration into hard metal sheets.
the effects of tool rotation speeds on the formation of the interfacial microstructures and the mechanical properties of Al Cu joints fabricated by FSW.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high rotation speed FSLW without tool penetration into hard materials is a feasible way to improve the joint properties of dissimilar materials.

high rotation speeds can be used to fabricate the Al Cu joints without tool penetration into hard Cu sheets, and the joints exhibit better mechanical properties than those produced at lower rotation speeds.

the formation of the composite like and layered structures at the Al Cu interface is mainly attributed to the different material flow characteristics and the tool/workpiece interactions at high rotation speeds during friction stir lap joining of dissimilar materials without tool penetration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the high rotation speed friction stirring process without tool penetration into workpieces is an effective method to produce high quality dissimilar metal joints.

the tool penetration into the Cu sheet is not required to form a sound Al Cu joint by friction stir lap welding at high rotation speeds, which is beneficial to the application of the friction stir welding technology to the lap joints of Al and Cu sheets.

a novel approach to friction stir lap welding dissimilar materials without tool penetration into hard materials is successfully proposed, which can be applied to other dissimilar materials with large difference in the mechanical properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high rotation speeds can weaken tool/workpiece interaction and improve the joint properties of friction stir lap welding dissimilar materials without tool penetration into hard lower sheets.
high rotation speeds can weaken tool workpiece interaction during friction lap welding of dissimilarity materials.
the tool penetration into the softer material is unnecessary during friction stir lap welded dissimilar metals, and high rotation speed is a feasible way to improve the joint properties.
